text:
alice: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the INT8 serving profile after yesterday's rollout. Canary p50 jumped from ~28ms to ~62ms on short-seq workloads. :eyes:
ben: Ugh. Is that across all models or a specific family?
alice: Short Llama-ish models (seq<=128) mostly. Long seqs look fine. Throughput down ~12% on the canary cluster. CI perf job also flagged it: perf-bot posted numbers.
perf-bot: [automated] quant-ci: baseline p50=28.4ms -> canary p50=61.7ms; p99 increased from 143ms -> 225ms. throughput -12%.
ben: I ran a quick perf map on a canary pod. Top hotspots are in the dequantize path — lots of small memcpy and elementwise convert ops. Kernel selector appears to be falling back to the generic float kernel for many layers.
carla: That sounds like the change merged in PR#7421 (kernel-selector tweak for affinity). We added a heuristic to prefer fused kernels only for seq>=256 to avoid memory blowouts. Maybe too conservative?
dmitri: I started a git bisect locally. First failing commit points at merge 0a1b2c3 (PR#7421). Reproduced with our microbench: `./bench --profile=int8 --seq=64 --iters=500`.
alece: (typo in name, should be alice)
alice: @dmitri nice, can you paste the exact bisect range?
dmitri: Bisect log: good @ 0f9eaa (pre-merge), bad @ 3c7b9f (post-merge). Culprit is commit 0a1b2c3 introducing "prefer_fused_for_large_seq" gating + change to kernel preference order.
ben: I attached a tiny flame diff: lots more time in `dequant_copy_nchw` and `to_float32` helpers. Previously the int8 fused decode path handled the convert in-kernel; now it does an explicit dequant->float memcpy before calling the generic kernel.
eva: Could this be KV cache related? The canary traces show more cache misses on short sequences because the new batching heuristic coalesces different seq lengths, so cache locality is worse.
ben: Good point — profiler shows increased L1/L2 misses concurrent with the dequant spikes. Not purely an allocator bug.
carla: Two paths to mitigate quickly: revert the preference change (safest) or flip a runtime flag to force fused kernels for seq<256 for the int8 profile.
dmitri: I can open a rollback PR, but we should be able to hotfix with config. There's a feature flag `runtime.kernel_selector.experimental` that was shipped but off — looks like we accidentally enabled it in canary for testing.
alece: (again typo)
alice: If it's a flag flip we should do that first on canary to confirm. Please coordinate with infra.
dmitri: Patching canary now: `kubectl set env deploy/runner KERNEL_SELECTOR_PREF=fused-shortseq --namespace=canary`
devops-bot: [deploy] Updated deployment/runner in canary namespace — restarted 4 pods (rolling).
perf-bot: [automated] canary-run-2: p50=31.2ms, p99=150ms, throughput -1.8% -> improvement but not fully back to baseline.
ben: After the flag flip, dequant memcpy time reduced ~70% but still seeing some generic kernel falls for a subset of layers. Kernel selector still prefers generic for layers with sparsely populated params due to memory heuristics.
eva: I dug into KV cache traces — batch coalescer is producing mixed-length batches more often when kernel preferences change, causing extra KV lookups per request (less reuse). That amplifies the dequant cost on short user requests.
carla: Proposed plan: 1) revert PR#7421 entirely in main (short-term) 2) open a follow-up to rework the heuristic to consider per-layer memory vs compute tradeoff and keep fused int8 for seq<=128 for now 3) add a CI perf test specifically for int8 short-seq mixes
ben: Also file an instrumentation task to add microbench assertions around "zero-copy dequant path" — if path introduces an extra memcpy we should fail CI.
dmitri: Agreed. I'll draft rollback PR now and tag @carla for the follow-up.
alece: (still typo)
alice: Nice. Can someone post the microbench command we should run on CI so SRE can add it to the perf job?
ben: Use: `./bench --model=llama-7b --profile=int8 --seq=64 --batch=8 --iters=1000 --capture=alloc,mem,flame`
perf-bot: [link] flamegraph: https://perf.internal/graphs/1837654321/canary-dequant-diff (internal)
devops-bot: Canary rollback started for release v2.14. If rollback fails, will auto-revert.
carla: I'll prepare the rework RFC this afternoon. Need to include KV cache interaction and batching policy tests.
alice: Thanks all — priority P0 until rollback lands and perf stabilizes. :thumbsup:
